title: Retrieval Eval Gold Set (v1.1)
description: Retrieval-answer-eval-set §1.1/§1.4 — the v1.1 evolution of schemas/retrieval/gold_set.schema.json. v1.0 stays const-pinned + frozen; this file ships the additive shape change so the loader (lib/retrieval/gold_set.py) can validate either version against the schema matching the doc's schema_version. NEW vs v1.0: two question_type values (procedural — an ordered procedure in 1-2 chunks; multi_part — >= 2 enumerable parts, parts may be deliberately partially covered); optional per-question fields expected_key_points (operator-reviewed claim-level completeness points), parts[] (required iff multi_part — each part covered/uncovered, uncovered parts carry an absence_note for the ws3.v2 completeness probes), expected_citation_population (source/course/both/any — for union corpora that mix original-document chunks with generated course-page chunks), objective_refs (TO-NN/CO-NN authored cross-check), difficulty (easy/medium/hard), synthesis_scope (within_week/across_weeks for conceptual_synthesis + multi_part); and an optional anchor.content_sha256 (normalized chunk-text hash at authoring) — the O(1) re-resolution key the gold-repin ladder (lib/retrieval/gold_repin.py) uses to survive a pure chunk-id renumber (e.g. a union-corpus rebuild). text_quote + item_path remain the fallback anchors. Validated by lib/retrieval/gold_set.py::validate_gold_set + schemas/tests/test_gold_set_schema_v1_1.py.

schema_version.description: Gold-set schema version. Const-pinned to 1.1 in this file; the loader selects the schema whose const matches the doc's schema_version.

course_slug.description: LibV2 course slug this gold set is authored for. Matches the private directory under LibV2/courses/.

chunkset.description: Pins WHICH chunkset the question chunk_ids reference. The kind selects the on-disk chunkset directory; chunks_path is course-dir-relative; chunks_sha256 is the freeze pin the loader recomputes and the eval harness hard-errors on.

kind.description: Chunkset kind. 'semantik' -> semantik_chunks/chunks.jsonl (current staged-conversion layout); 'imscc' -> imscc_chunks/chunks.jsonl; 'dart' -> legacy dart_chunks/chunks.jsonl read-fallback; 'corpus' -> the union corpus/chunks.jsonl (generated course pages + original-textbook chunks).

chunks_path.description: Path to the pinned chunks.jsonl, relative to the course dir (e.g. 'corpus/chunks.jsonl').

chunks_sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex, lowercase) of the pinned chunks.jsonl at authoring time. The loader recomputes the on-disk SHA and emits GOLD_SET_CHUNKSET_SHA_MISMATCH (critical) on disagreement — eval refuses to run against a corpus that has drifted from the bytes the gold set was authored against. Re-pin with `libv2 gold-repin`.

authored_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp recording when the gold set was authored.

frozen.description: v1-freeze flag. False for seed/draft gold sets; flips true once the gold set is operator-reviewed and frozen. The loader refuses mutation-mode operations (incl. gold-repin) on a frozen set without --unfreeze-for-repin.

_operator_note.description: Optional free-text note to the operator (e.g. the scale-up-to-50/freeze hand-off, or a single-corpus provenance caveat).

questions.description: The gold-set questions. Each binds question text + type to >= 1 relevant passage, with at least one passage marked relevance:primary.

allOf.description: parts[] is required iff question_type is multi_part.

question_id.description: Gold-question id. Pattern gq-<course_slug>-NNNN (4-digit zero-padded ordinal). Loader enforces uniqueness within the set (GOLD_SET_DUPLICATE_QUESTION_ID).

question_text.description: The question a retriever must answer. Min 10 chars.

question_type.description: Question taxonomy (v1.1). factual_recall: a verbatim fact in one chunk. procedural: an ordered procedure in 1-2 chunks (key points are the steps). conceptual_synthesis: answer spans >= 2 chunks. multi_part: >= 2 enumerable parts (the parts[] block is required; parts may be deliberately partially covered). where_covered: 'where does the course cover X'.

synthesis_scope.description: Optional (conceptual_synthesis + multi_part): whether the relevant passages live in one content week or span multiple. Cross-checked by the coverage report against the relevant passages' item_path weeks.

difficulty.description: Optional authored difficulty. easy = verbatim in one chunk; medium = paraphrase or 2-chunk join; hard = >= 3 chunks, across-weeks, or a partially-covered multi_part. Cross-checked by the coverage report (~40/40/20 target).

phrasing.description: Optional learner-phrasing axis (default 'canonical' when absent). canonical: a well-formed textbook-style question ('What is the standard form of a linear equation?'). colloquial: a casual/bare learner voice ('what is the greatest common factor?', 'what's the quadratic formula and when to use it?'). malformed: realistic learner typos / doubled articles / dropped words that stay humanly interpretable ('what is a the standard form?'). The grounded eval (lib/retrieval/grounded_eval.py) slices answerability by this value so an operator can see at a glance whether colloquial / malformed reasonable questions still pass. Provenance/analysis only — never affects per-question scoring.

objective_refs.description: Optional authored learning-objective ids (TO-NN / CO-NN) this question exercises. Cross-checked by the coverage report against the course objectives map.

expected_citation_population.description: Optional (default 'any'): which corpus population the answer's citations should be drawn from on a union corpus. 'source' = the original document (textbook chunks, block + PDF-page provenance); 'course' = the generated course pages; 'both' = a synthesis that must cite each; 'any' = no constraint.

expected_key_points.description: Optional 2-6 operator-reviewed key points for claim-level completeness scoring (shingle/coverage and/or NLI at eval time). Supersedes the unscored answer_note for new questions.

parts.description: Required iff question_type is multi_part: the enumerable parts. covered:false parts carry an absence_note documenting the deliberately-uncovered part (the ws3.v2 completeness probes — the pipeline must correctly flag the absent part, not invent it).

allOf.description: absence_note is required iff covered is false.

part_id.description: Stable id of the part within the question (e.g. 'a', 'b', 'p1').

covered.description: True when the corpus answers this part (relevant_passage_refs anchor it). False for a deliberately-uncovered completeness probe.

relevant_passage_refs.description: Optional chunk_ids (subset of the question's relevant_passages) that answer this part. Present for covered parts.

absence_note.description: Required iff covered:false — the human rationale (>= 20 chars) for why the corpus does not cover this part, plus a note that the dry-run confirmed the absence.

relevant_passages.description: Chunks that answer the question. At least one MUST have relevance:primary (enforced via `contains`).

chunk_id.description: Chunk id in the pinned chunkset. Loader verifies it exists (GOLD_SET_UNKNOWN_CHUNK_ID).

relevance.description: primary: directly answers the question. supporting: contributes context (synthesis / where_covered / multi_part companion passages).

anchor.description: Chunkset-independent re-resolution anchor. text_quote keeps the gold answer matchable after any future re-chunk; content_sha256 (v1.1) is the O(1) exact key when present.

item_path.description: Copied from chunk.source.item_path — the source page the chunk derives from.

section_heading.description: Optional human-readable section locator copied from chunk.source.section_heading.

text_quote.description: Verbatim substring of chunk.text carrying the answer, >= 40 chars. The loader verifies normalized containment in the cited chunk (GOLD_SET_QUOTE_NOT_IN_CHUNK).

content_sha256.description: Optional (v1.1): SHA-256 of the cited chunk's normalized text (lib/retrieval/gold_set.py::chunk_content_sha256 = sha256 of normalize_ws(text).lower()) at authoring. The gold-repin ladder resolves by this exact hash FIRST (survives a pure renumber / union rebuild), falling back to text_quote then item_path. Backfilled by `libv2 gold-repin` on every resolved passage.

answer_note.description: Optional free-text gist of the expected answer (eval aid; superseded by expected_key_points for new questions).

authoring.description: Provenance of this question. Seed/draft questions are reviewed_by:PENDING_REVIEW until operator review backfills the reviewer and the set freezes.

method.description: How the question was authored. manual: hand-authored / seeded from a live query. llm_assisted: drafted with the license-clean local provider (still operator-reviewed before freeze).

author.description: @handle or tool id (model+prompt-version) of the author.

reviewed_by.description: @handle of the reviewer, or PENDING_REVIEW for un-reviewed seed/draft questions.

status.description: Authoring lifecycle. seed: deterministic executor-authored starter. draft: in-progress (incl. a gold-repin-parked unresolved question). reviewed: operator-approved (freeze prerequisite).

template.description: Optional (llm_assisted only): which gold-candidate drafting arm produced the question. stratified: the §1.2 stratified sampler; definition: a glossary-term definition question; worked_example: a Problem/Solution/Step procedural question; both_population: a synthesis question pairing a course-population chunk with a source-population chunk on the same concept (expected_citation_population=both). The learner_intent arms (conceptual_why / comparative / example_seeking / notation_symbol / word_problem) each mine the matching corpus shape; the phrasing arms (phrasing_malformed / phrasing_colloquial) are paraphrase variants of a canonical question that reuse its relevant_passages verbatim. Provenance only — never affects eval scoring.
